steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Eh, now that you mention it, this is starting to ring a bell.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: A few years ago, I participated in a couple Dome design contests with him and Catch.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Master Finch had just left not too long before that, and our rising new stars both wanted to prove themselves with their Dome renovation plans.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Catch was an incessant one at the meetings. He kept selling his ideas and the advantages of his design.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: As for Stitch, all he ever did was lay his designs on the table before standing aside. It seemed kind of like he would rather we see his ideas for ourselves instead of wasting his energy to explain them.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Some preferred Catch's detailed way of thinking, while others acknowledged Stitch's confidence, even egotism toward his own work. Both of them were undoubtedly rising stars.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: This rivalry continued for several years, and neither of them was able to truly obtain the recognition of the majority and get his designs passed.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Until one day... when Stitch stopped showing up.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Finch actually brought it up to me before back when he was still around. He told me he was worried about his student's future.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: But those problems you can fix by talking sense into him. He has to think things through himself and set his ego aside. Only then will he hear another opinion.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Otherwise, forget Catch. Not even someone as strong as Gavial could do anything about him.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Not even if Gavial really wanted to help him from the bottom of her heart?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: If there was a way around it, Finch would've tried it a long time ago.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: But... who knows? Catch and Gavial couldn't be more different, personality-wise. If the two of them tried to help him together, a miracle might just happen.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: *sigh*, these are Zumama's friends. It's such a pain when I can't just wreck them.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hmm? Okay, you guys know Zumama, right? I'm her friend.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Zumama... Confirming identity. Zumama's friend: Gavial.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Zumama told us we can't hurt Gavial.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: We won't hurt Gavial.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Haha, I saw you guys chumming together and thought you were really hitting it off. Didn't expect mentioning her name to actually do anything.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Gah!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Help me surround him, won't you?

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: We cannot allow Zeruertza's citizens come to harm.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Relax, I'm just taking him where he should be.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Understood. We trust Gavial. We will help Gavial.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Out of my way!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Stitch Canvas, I've got something to ask you.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I have nothing more to say to you!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You've said plenty, but in the end, do you hate the people of Zeruertza?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: No, you don't have to answer.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: If you hated them, then you should've stayed on the surface after you made it there. You could've hid the danger your tribe is facing.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But you told us anyway.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You didn't want to fix the Dome, but you couldn't give this place up. That's why you brought Tomimi and Inam down here.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Yeah, so what?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm just curious.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Have you ever talked to the ones who voted against you and asked them why they didn't like your proposal?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: No... I haven't.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah, I thought so. Just like you definitely haven't ever told anyone the stuff you just said.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: And actually, you still haven't told me how you truly feel.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I know. Some things are difficult to bring up.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I have lots of patients who would rather die than open up.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: They don't want to make trouble for people, they don't think anyone understands them, or they're just too stubborn to actually say it... You name it, I've seen it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But whatever the deal is, if you keep it to yourself all the way to the day you die, no one's going to know.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm not gonna say you've done anything wrong.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But I need you to give it a shot.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: How I really feel? Not even I know how I really feel anymore!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Then I've gotta at least...
Hold up!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Gavial, wait, please.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Catch? What are you doing here?
The forum is dead silent.
All the Durins are attentively listening to Avdotya tell her story.
Though her story starts off warm, it slowly deteriorates into something more sinister as it progresses.
When the story gets going, the audience holds their collective breaths, only for Avdotya to explain how she survived, sending out a collective sigh of relief.
But that's only where it starts, it's the beginning of her hardships and tribulations, and she goes through much more as she recounts the story.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: When I reached the end of the cave... for a moment, I thought my eyes were deceiving me.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Had it not been a golden, shining lift, I would've mistaken it for a staircase carrying me to death.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: At that very moment, I even felt joy. I thought my hardships were coming to an end.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I thought I could enjoy a moment of respite within death's embrace.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I never expected that lift would open the door to a new life.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And that was everything I went through before I made it underground.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: This is the life on the surface that I can share with you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: It's hardly what you would call a wonderful one.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But, looking back, it wasn't actually as hard as I remember it

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Anyway, I'm sure that the smarter ones among you already know what I'm getting at.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: It's true.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Based on our discussions, we've arrived at three possible evacuation plans.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: First, we could evacuate via the tunnels.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: According to the calculations, even if we start evacuating right now as quickly as we can, we will likely only be able to evacuate seventy percent of our population to our sibling city on the other end before the explosion.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: If that is the plan we are going with, we must start immediately, without delay.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The second plan would require us to immediately use all our resources to excavate in the opposite direction of the tunnel. In other words, dig toward the hole on the other side and open up a safe shelter for our temporary refuge.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: As it stands, this proposal gives us a higher survival rate than the previous one, but the tunnel is our only connection to other cities.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The disaster will destroy most of our facilities, and under those circumstances, let's not mention the issue of whether this newly-excavated shelter will be able to hold everyone in the city...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Even if we managed to save everyone, it's questionable that we would last much longer after disaster strikes.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: As for the third proposal... It takes us to the surface.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The industrial representative estimates that after a short extension, the lift will be able to take everyone in the city to the caves above before the explosion happens.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The guests who arrived not too long ago are from the lands directly above Zeruertza.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: That area is a lush rainforest named Acahualla, and as their administrators, they are willing to provide all Zeruertzans living space and other assistance.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: When the crisis is over, after we settle down, we can choose to return to this place or make other arrangements.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: So far, the third proposal carries the least risk and is the most likely to keep everyone alive.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: However, we must make a decision that might just be unprecedented for the Durin people—

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: We must head for the surface.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: That is also the reason why I told you my story.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: We still have other options available, and I don't want to influence your decision.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Allow my story to help you determine for yourselves.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Okay. Per usual, we will vote on the three proposals in ten minutes.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I have something I need to talk to Stitch about.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Stitch, I...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Isn't it just perfect that you're in charge of the dome?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You're the design representative, and everyone loves you. With you in charge of the new dome design, everyone's going to be happy with the result.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: This rivalry we've had for all these years? You've won it fair and square.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Oh, that's not what I'm here for.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I'm here to say goodbye.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: You see, I've only been ACTING design representative since Master Finch left us.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: And after I took up the burden, I gradually began to think that maybe my skills weren't up to the task.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Actually, I've been thinking about leaving to look for Master Finch. I mean, he's the only one who can really be our design representative.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: And after I'm gone, as his disciple, you're the most suitable one to take the job.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I just went back to the design department and handed my work over to the others, and I'm ready to get my things packed and leave.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: But why now?!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I heard we're all going to the surface. I caught Avdotya's speech when I passed by the forum just now.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I'm sure the proposal will end up passing.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But Master Finch should be hiding out in some other Durin city. That's why, while it's still possible, I want to settle down in the one next door before I figure out my next steps.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: So, sorry, buddy. I probably won't get to help with the dome's design.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You... You think I'd be happy about this?!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But I really think you are up to the task.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: All you need is a chance to let people get to know you. Seriously.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: How dare you?!
In his anger, Stitch raises his fist against Catch.
But it stops in its tracks midair, before falling down powerlessly.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I know Master Finch left because he wanted me to become independent.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: And I know you're doing this because you want me to give it another shot.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Gavial, too. I know all of you are doing this out of the kindness of your hearts.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Of course I know!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: But... Master Finch, you, and Gavial... Why do you have to force me down this path?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Why can't all of you just leave me alone?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Why can't you just let me keep hiding?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Why do all of you have to be so kind?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Why?!
Catch quietly picks up the design sketch next to him and hands it to Stitch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Because you tried so hard.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: You can do much better. I know it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Since when do you need a reason to be kind?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: And since when do you need a reason to want to keep someone from falling like that?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Now, get up.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Stop crying.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: First, you lied to my tribesmen, and now you're making trouble for all kinds of people.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So, I'm going to sock you.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Grit your teeth. It won't hurt too bad.
Stitch looks at Gavial's fist.
In an instant, many things flash through his mind.
The joy he felt when he listened to his teacher's lectures.
The hatred he felt when his teacher left.
The disappointment he felt every time he walked out of the design department after losing a design contest.
Before he knew it, whenever he looked at the dome above him, it was anger that he felt, not excitement.
He thought the feeling was his alone and that not only could no one understand him, he did not need to be understood by anyone.
But, at this very moment, now that he's finally learned that there are those who truly want to understand him and help him...
He realizes that perhaps it is time to set that something down.
He then thinks to himself... he should take this punch.
'Bam!'
Yet, even though he was anticipating the pain, he doesn't feel a thing.
He looks down to find a deep, fist-sized pit in the table.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hah, now you're scared?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Relax, my fist's only for the bad guys.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You're not a bad guy. You're just a knucklehead. Why should I beat you up?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You're the knucklehead!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Well, look at you. In such a good mood that you can still talk back, huh?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So how about it? Wanna come along now?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Okay, let us proceed with the voting.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: If you are voting for the first proposal, please raise your hand.
A sparse number of hands go up around the forum.
Those with their hands up appear very calm, as though they've made up their minds, even though they know there wouldn't be many people voting for this measure.
And Avdotya knows that those who would vote for this proposal are always the ones who are willing to give their lives.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Record keeper, please record the number of votes for the first proposal.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Okay, please put your hands down.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: If you are voting for the second proposal, please raise your hand.
This time, there are a lot of people with their hands up. Some of them even have bottles in them.
Most of them have rather sturdy builds. Undoubtedly, they are very confident in their excavation skills.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Record keeper, please record the number of votes for the second proposal.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Okay, please put your hands down.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: If you are voting for the third proposal, please raise your hand.
The forum is dead silent.
No one has a hand up.
Avdotya knows that this outcome is only to be expected. Heading to the surface is a big decision, and her speech alone could hardly be enough to persuade them.
When she looks at the Durins whispering among themselves, she knows that her story has had no effect on them.
The Durins are not afraid. All they need is an opportunity.
They still need a push.
She also feels guilt deep in her heart.
The old her definitely would have been leading the opposition against moving to the surface.
But now she is doing other Durins' work for this.
Her guilty feelings quickly disappear, as she knows she is doing what is right.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I have a few things to add about going to the surface.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Acahualla is a humid rainforest. It is hot there, no matter the time of the year.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Even without any temperature control, we should still be able to get used to life there.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Besides, Acahualla is rich in lake water resources and is home to a natural waterfall. In other words, it's an all-natural 'Great Aquapit.'

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Furthermore, Acahualla also has a large amount of mineral resources and land. If we wish to, we can build a new city there.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Of course, we will also have the pride of Zeruertza, a new landmark that will once again put smiles on everyone's faces!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Though we will have to discuss this with Acahualla's leader before we can make a decision.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Inam will agree to it.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Gavial?!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hey, Avdotya, look who I brought here.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Hm? Who is it?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: It's Stitch. I see you guys are pretty much done with that discussion. So, the dome repair's next, right?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Guess I came at just the right time?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You came at a terrible time!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh, alright. I mean, I may not be the leader of Acahualla, but let me say this on her behalf. Acahualla welcomes you all!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Get off the stage!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hey, I got more to say!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: No way!

steps.name: Heartened Durin
steps.text: It's true, Gavial and the surface-dwellers are all interesting.

steps.name: Rational Durin
steps.text: Word. Besides, not only are they kind, they're strong, too. Making friends with them sounds like a fine idea.

steps.name: Cheerful Durin
steps.text: I think so, too! Besides, they've got a bigger 'Great Aquapit' in Acahualla! What could be better?

steps.name: Rational Durin
steps.text: But let's calm down and think it through. This is going to affect the future of the whole Durin race.

steps.name: Heartened Durin
steps.text: I don't see anything wrong with that future though.

steps.name: Cheerful Durin
steps.text: Right, I'm with ya. I mean, even though a lot of bad things happened on the surface in Avdotya's story, just like we've always heard—

steps.name: Rational Durin
steps.text: But if all those bad things shaped Avdotya into the kind person that she is, I don't think there's anything to be afraid of.

steps.name: Cheerful Durin
steps.text: Besides, I've heard rumors that 'Stranger Things' is still running on the surface!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Gavial, do you know how much time and effort I spent to prepare for this moment?!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: What if they decide to stay down here because you had to butt in?!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hm... but I just took a look around, and all of them seem to be looking forward to it. They're gonna vote for it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You persuaded them already.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: How can you always be so optimistic...?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: By the way, Gavial, how is Stitch doing?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: He says he's willing to give it a shot.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hm? Where did he go?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I saw him in the forum. That's why I'm asking.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: And looking at him now, it looks like he's really going to do it.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Let me give him a hand, then.
The crowd of the forum is bubbling with talk of going to the surface.
This seems to have nothing to do with him. He should have gone inside with Gavial. He has never been comfortable with situations like this to begin with.
But he stays where he is.
He knows he isn't afraid.
He knows that there is an urge inside of him to say something.
But he has no idea how to begin.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Right, I have a piece of regrettable news I forgot to share.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: After he learned of Zeruertza's impending disaster, our design representative, Catch Lightrace, has decided to resign from his position and part ways with us for the moment.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: He's going to seek out our previous design representative, Master Finch Canvas, whose whereabouts are unknown.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I understand and respect his decision.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Furthermore, before he left, he appointed Master Finch's disciple, Stitch Canvas to take his position.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: And I know better than anyone that Stitch Canvas is a talented architect. Which is why I accepted this request.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Now, let's invite him up here to say a few words.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Stitch, the floor is yours.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I... I'm aware you don't really know who I am... Just that my teacher is the famous Finch Canvas.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: M-My style is very different from my teacher's. His is more about resisting materialism, while mine is more leaning toward—

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Sorry, that's not what I wanted to say.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I want to talk about the proposal, the one about going to the surface.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I know this isn't an easy decision to make.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: But I think it's the safest option available.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: And if we choose this plan, we will still have time to dress our doomed city.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: There's not much that I can do, but I'm willing to spend the last bit of time we have to come up with a plan to repair the dome.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: And, if at all possible, I want to make the dome even sturdier.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Even though it's impossible to keep an active Originium vein from exploding, that should still buy us some time.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: So please, everyone. Let's head to the surface. I'm sure my teacher... would've wanted it too.
The audience is silent.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: (Quietly) Master Edge, did I say something wrong?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: No, you did very well. Good kid. I knew you could do it.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Very well, then. Let's take the votes again for the third proposal.
As though Stitch's speech has unified their opinions, the very next moment, the Durins start raising their hands one by one.
All of them are chanting something different; Stitch is unable to make it out.
But he can just barely hear some of them complimenting him.
He notices that, on a platform high up above in the distance, Catch is faintly waving to seemingly congratulate him.
It feels as though an electric current suddenly surges through him.
For the first time, he realizes just how exhilarating it feels to be acknowledged.
